reason: I’ll follow the only available combination to begin supplying the muscle fibers for continued work.
expectation: I expect the sugar to provide fuel for the fibers, though oxygen may also be needed.

effect: The sugar begins producing ATP in the cell fluid and leaves fuel for mitochondria, so oxygen looks like the next supply to add.
reaction: It is useful to see the machinery from the previous chapter doing work.
reason: Oxygen is the only offered combination and should help the muscle fibers continue producing ATP.
expectation: I expect oxygen to help the mitochondria use the partly processed fuel to replenish more ATP.

effect: Oxygen helps the fibers replenish ATP from fuel, supporting continued pulling. The goal now is to organize them into opposing muscles.
reaction: The distinction between oxygen and fuel clarifies how the continuing cycle works.
reason: Wrapping the fibers is the only offered combination and seems useful for organizing them into muscles.
expectation: I expect the wrapping to bundle the fibers into a muscle assembly, though I’m unsure how the two opposing groups will form.

effect: The wrapping organizes fibers into bundles and carries their tension toward the muscle ends, so tendons seem like the next connection.
reaction: The explanation makes the supporting material’s purpose clear.
reason: I’ll add the front tendons to begin forming one of the opposing muscle groups.
expectation: I expect a front muscle group with tendons that can eventually attach to a framework.

alternatives.reason: The rear tendons seem equally relevant, but I chose to start with the front group.

effect: The front tendons formed bending muscles that can pull on bones once the framework is arranged; the opposite muscle group still needs to be made.
reaction: The connection between tendon placement and bending the elbow is clear.
reason: I’ll use the only offered combination to form the opposing muscle group.
expectation: I expect the rear tendons and bundles to form muscles that can straighten the elbow once attached to the framework.

effect: The rear tendons formed the straightening muscles, completing the opposing groups; their eventual movements depend on where they attach.
reaction: The paired bending and straightening pulls are satisfying, though the framework is still to come.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen was most worthwhile because the result connected fuel, ATP replenishment and muscle pulling, while explaining that oxygen is not itself food or energy.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the rear tendons was fairly predictable after making the bending muscles, though it completed the opposing pair.

surprise.text: I was interested that sugar processing makes some ATP in the watery cell interior before mitochondria use the partly processed fuel.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless. Choosing front before rear was arbitrary because both tendon options seemed equally relevant.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the opposing muscles attach to a framework and produce movement; the connection from cellular work to an acting arm interests me.
